admin.pin.title: Set or clear a PIN
admin.pin.heading: Set a PIN for “%s”
admin.pin.explain: This replaces the PIN on “%s”, and the old one stops working at once. Submit it empty to cancel the PIN — after that, anyone on your LAN can open this profile.
admin.pin.field: New PIN (4-6 digits; leave empty to cancel it)
admin.delete.title: Delete profile
admin.delete.heading: Delete “%s”?
admin.delete.explain: %d bookmarks and %d snapshots will be deleted, and they cannot be brought back. Reverting to an earlier version will not save them either, because the snapshots go with the profile. The record of who changed what, and when, stays.
import.heading: Import bookmarks from your browser
import.explain: A browser export is a single HTML file. Pick it and there are two buttons: “Import now” writes it straight in, and “Show what this would import” gives you a report first. Both ways put in exactly the same thing — importing is only open to a profile with no bookmarks at all, and addresses a page cannot open (the browser’s own trash, `javascript:` links) do not come across. If anything is left out, the finishing page names each one.
import.notice.blocked: This profile already has %d bookmarks. Import is only open to a profile with none — to add to a list you already have, use the “+ Add” button on the page.
import.notice.unreadable: That upload could not be read. The usual cause is that it is over 8 MB, but a damaged file does it too. Try another one.
import.notice.toolarge: That file cannot be read, or it is over 8 MB.
import.explainStep: A browser export is a single HTML file. In Chrome or Edge: bookmark manager, then the three dots at the top right, then Export bookmarks. In Firefox: Bookmarks, Manage bookmarks, Import and Backup, Export to HTML. What gets imported goes into this profile only.
admin.disable.explain.on: Once disabled, “%s” stays shut even with the right PIN and no longer appears on the picker. Not one byte of its bookmarks or snapshots changes, and you can enable it again at any time.
admin.disable.explain.off: Once enabled, “%s” can be opened with its PIN again and reappears on the picker.
revert.choice.label: Version %d · %d bookmarks
revert.now.unreadable: Now: this one cannot be read (its data file is broken), which is exactly when reverting is the way out.
revert.title: Revert to an earlier version
revert.heading: Revert “%s” to an earlier version?
revert.explain.main: Reverting replaces this profile with the version you picked. Before anything changes, the current state is saved as a snapshot, so a wrong revert can be undone by reverting again. A revert counts as a new change and adds a line to the history; it erases nothing. At most 50 snapshots are kept, and older ones are dropped.
revert.explain.unreadable: A further %d snapshots could not be read and are not listed.
revert.explain.noversions: This profile has no earlier version to revert to yet: one is saved before every change, so right now this is the only version there is.
